To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal antenna configuration depends on the ratio of the costs of implementing one antenna at the base station versus one antenna at the mobile, and that the optimal number of antennas at base stations and mobiles can be different for the uplink and the downlink.
the optimal number of antennas at mobile and base station are not the same for the uplink and the downlink.

the optimal number of antennas at base station is a function of the cost ratio of the base station to mobile station and signal to noise ratio, and that the optimal number at the mobile station is a function only of the signal-to-noise-ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of optimizing antenna configuration in a multiple-input/multiplex-out system, with a linear combination of uplink and down link capacity as the objective function.
the problem of optimizing the number of antennas to be used at the base station (BS) and the mobile station (MS) in a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication system.
the optimization of antenna configuration for multiple-input/multiple- output (MIMO) systems in the presence of cost constraints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of antennas to be implemented at the base station should increase with signal-to-noiseratio, while the number of antennas implemented at the mobile should be kept constant.
, for a wide range of SNR and cost ratio, the optimum number of base station antennas should be at least twice that of the optimum number of mobile antennas.

the optimal antenna configuration is a function of the ratio of the cost of an antenna at the base station relative to that of an antenna at mobile, the signal-to-noise ratios at the base station, and at the mobile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a fixed cost ratio of the base station to mobile antennas, the ratio of the base antennas to mobile antennas increases with signal-to-noiseratio.
the optimal number of antennas at both ends of the link increases with SNR and cost ratio.

the number of antennas should be chosen at both the transmitter and the receiver so as to maximize the total system capacity, which in general is a function of the number of transmit antennas and receive antennas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal number of antennas at base station and mobile are not the same for the two cases of unequal and equal cost of implementing antennas at base station or mobile.
the optimal number of antennas at base station and at mobile are different when the costs of antennas at base stations and at mobiles are different.
, in order to maximize system capacity, the ratio of the base station to mobile antennas should decrease as the cost ratio decreases and the signal-to-noise-ratio increases.
